title: Void Ending in a Sextile to Mercury
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The sextile is one of the two friendly aspects. Picatrix ties the Moon to the fortunes by trine and sextile whenever a work is meant to prosper, and grades the sextile as the aspect of moderate friendship: the signs it joins are kin in action but not in passion, so the concord between them is a lukewarm one.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a sextile to Mercury, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his quicksilver turn of mind. Mercury is intellect's planet: learning, dialectic, geometry, astronomy, writing, and the reading of tongues, with every craft found by subtle talent under his governance. He rules the tongue, the brain, and the sensory memory, and quicksilver among the metals. The electional doctrine guards him closely: a work founded on Mercury must not find him retrograde, burning in the Sun's beams, or under an unfortunate planet's gaze.
